key_insight: Charge disproportionation restores directional cobalt orbital magnetism in layered polar metal Sr₃Co₂O₇, producing giant magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: The mechanism suggests a design route toward rare-earth-free permanent magnets, rather than AI or solar-cell applications.
method: Comparison of polar and centrosymmetric structures.
evidence_signal: Calculations favor in-plane [110] magnetization over [001] by 234.0 meV per cell, while the centrosymmetric reference shows strongly reduced anisotropy.
watch_item: The computational findings require experimental validation; large anisotropy alone does not establish practical permanent-magnet performance.
paper_title: Giant magnetic anisotropy in layered polar metal Sr$_3$Co$_2$O$_7$ from Charge-disproportionation orbital unquenching
